summary: Same storm: identical scrolling blue rain comb (same 10 px/s drift, same spacing law shape), statistically identical amber sparkles and the same white cloud-glow block at the strip end — but the port's lightning fires ~4-5x more often for ~1/7 the duration at the harness rate, its glow cycle runs 1.65x fast, all three element colours are shifted, and its one dial is renamed, direction-inverted and range-compressed.
observations: Rig: strip, 60 px. Both sides compile and run clean (no compile/runtime errors, wantsSensors false on both). Neither side dies, saturates or drifts: over --skip 100 --seconds 20 both sit at meanBrightness ~44, and over a 240 s / 10 fps survey the per-sixth mean brightness is flat on both (orig 39.6/49.9/48.6/44.6/48.3/44.1, port 48.0/49.6/45.7/47.9/47.9/45.4). No mode/regime structure on either side beyond the glow cycle and the lightning events.

Both sides layer exactly three elements over black: (1) a scrolling comb of single-pixel rain drops, (2) sparse single-pixel warm sparkles, (3) a uniform white 'cloud glow' block occupying the last ~6-12 pixels of the strip whose brightness sawtooths up and holds. Plus whole-strip lightning flashes. Same element inventory, same layering order (the glow block is drawn on top of the flash on both sides).

RAIN GEOMETRY MATCHES EXACTLY. Both draw a perfectly regular comb (constant pixel spacing, not random drops) that scrolls toward index 0. At matched density (orig sliderSpeed=0.25, port sliderRainDensity=0 — both spacing 17) a 0.1 s-spaced dump gives orig comb offsets 17,16,15,14,13,12,11,10,9,8 and port 16,15,14,13,12,11,10,9,8,7 over t=0.1..1.0 s: both exactly -1 px per 0.1 s = -10 px/s, differing only by a 1-pixel phase offset. Speed is fps-invariant on BOTH (-10 px/s measured identically at 10, 20 and 40 fps), so no frame-rate coupling in the rain on either side.

SPARKLE STATISTICS MATCH EXACTLY. Over 115 samples spread across 30 s at default dials: orig 1.02 sparkles/frame (histogram 0:45 1:39 2:18 3:10 4:3), port 1.02/frame (0:41 1:38 2:28 3:6 4:1). Same rate, same distribution, same random single-pixel placement.

COLOUR SHIFTS (exact --dump RGB, both sides constant): rain drop orig (0,56,255) vs port (0,8,203) — the port's rain is a markedly darker, more saturated navy and visibly dimmer; sparkle orig (255,152,0) vs port (255,107,0) — the port's sparkles are redder; lightning flash orig (255,152,0), i.e. the SAME saturated amber as its own sparkles, vs port (255,190,114), a pale peach/white-hot. The port's overall colour balance shows in the stats: at --skip 100 --seconds 20, orig meanR/G/B = 51.2/44.8/35.5 vs port 38.2/35.1/57.8.

LIGHTNING RATE AND DURATION DIVERGE. At the default 20 fps over 120 s: orig 8 flashes (4/min), each lasting exactly 1.05 s (21 frames), inter-flash gaps all integer multiples of 1.05 s (3.15, 5.25, 9.45, 11.55, 15.75, 22.05) — i.e. the original runs a 21-frame storm tick and fires on a tick. Port over the same 120 s: 28 flashes (14/min), each exactly 0.15 s (3 frames), gaps continuous (0.50 .. 6.30 s, no quantisation). Seed-robust: seed 7 gives orig 4 vs port 20 flashes/60 s, seed 1234 gives orig 3 vs port 18, durations unchanged at 1.05 s vs 0.15 s.

ROOT CAUSE OF THE LIGHTNING GAP IS A FRAME-COUPLING MISMATCH, and it runs the opposite way to the usual bug: the ORIGINAL is frame-counted, the PORT is time-based. Orig flash duration is 21 rendered frames at every rate (2.1 s at 10 fps, 1.05 s at 20 fps, 0.53 s at 40 fps) and its rate scales with fps (2/min at 10 fps, 4/min at 20 fps, 8/min at 40 fps). Port duration holds at ~0.13-0.20 s and its rate holds at ~14-18/min across 10/20/40 fps. The two sides would agree near ~80 fps on rate and ~140 fps on duration, so the port's absolute time constants are in the ballpark of the original running at real-hardware frame rates — but at the harness's pinned 20 fps the visible result is 4-5x too many flashes, each ~7x too brief, and the original's flash reads as a sustained one-second amber wash where the port's reads as a fast white strobe.

CLOUD-GLOW CYCLE IS 1.65x TOO FAST, and this one is NOT an fps artefact — measured from the glow block's brightness sawtooth resets with rain suppressed, orig period = 6.50 s and port = 3.95 s at 10, 20 AND 40 fps alike. Orig: floor 129, ramps +38.8 counts/s to 255 in ~3.25 s, then holds at 255 for ~3.25 s (50% duty). Port: floor ~90, ramps +64 counts/s to 254 in ~2.6 s, then holds ~1.35 s (~35% duty). Port also never reaches full white (254 vs 255).

Glow block size: the block's length jitters randomly frame to frame on both sides, but the port's is consistently ~1.6 px shorter — orig length histogram over 120 samples {7:9, 8:17, 9:21, 10:21, 11:27, 12:25}, avg 9.96 px; port {6:9, 7:29, 8:24, 9:29, 10:29}, avg 8.33 px.

CONTROL-SURFACE MISMATCH: the original exposes one slider named `sliderSpeed` (label 'Speed'); the port exposes one slider named `sliderRainDensity` (label 'RainDensity'). Same kind and count, different name — so a --controls string written for one side silently no-ops on the other.

UNTOUCHED DEFAULTS DIVERGE ON RAIN. With no control values applied the original draws NO rain at all (zero blue pixels in all 120 samples across 30 s; only sparkles plus the glow block), while the port draws a spacing-6 comb, ~9 drops per frame — equivalent to orig sliderSpeed ~0.07. Untouched mean brightness happens to land close anyway (orig 43.9 vs port 43.7 over the late window) because the port's extra rain roughly offsets the original's longer/brighter lightning.

At matched rain density the two waterfalls are near-twins: `matched-sparse` (orig Speed=0.25 / port RainDensity=0, both spacing 17) shows the same diagonal streak slope, same spacing and the same sparkle scatter on both, with the only visible differences being the port's darker blue, its two flash lines in the 12 s window against the original's zero, and the faster glow sawtooth on the right edge.

dials.name: sliderSpeed (orig) / sliderRainDensity (port)
dials.origEffect: Live (probe maxDelta 42.3 / maxDeltaLit 71.1). Despite the name 'Speed' the observable effect is rain DENSITY: drop spacing is linear in the dial, spacing = 2 + 60*v — measured 2, 8, 14, 20, 26, 32, 38, 44, 50, 56, 62 px at v = 0, 0.1 ... 1.0. So v=0 is a dense period-2 comb filling the strip and v=1 is effectively a single drop. Scroll SPEED is unaffected (-9 to -10 px/s at every dial value), and flash rate/duration and glow period are unaffected (2 flashes per 40 s and a 6.55 s glow cycle at v = 0, 0.5 and 1 alike).
dials.portEffect: Live (probe maxDelta 19.4 / maxDeltaLit 36.0). Same physical effect — rain drop spacing — but INVERTED and range-compressed: spacing = 17, 15, 14, 12, 11, 9, 7, 6, 4, 3, 2 px at v = 0, 0.1 ... 1.0 (roughly 17 - 15*v). Scroll speed, flash rate/duration and glow period are all unaffected by the dial, as on the original.

feedback: Rename the control to match the original: it must be `sliderSpeed` with label 'Speed', not `sliderRainDensity`/'RainDensity'. A control-name mismatch means saved values and any UI written against the original don't carry over.

Invert and rescale the dial. The original's mapping is drop spacing = 2 + 60*sliderValue over a 60 px strip (dial 0 = densest, period-2 comb; dial 1 = one lone drop). The port's is spacing ~= 17 - 15*value (dial 1 = densest). The port's ENTIRE 0..1 range only reproduces the original's 0..0.25 — everything the original does above 0.25 (spacing 17 up to 62, i.e. genuinely sparse drizzle) is unreachable on the port. Fix the direction first, then widen the range so spacing spans 2..62.

The original's untouched default draws NO rain at all (spacing > 60); the port's untouched default draws spacing-6 rain. Whatever the port's slider-backed variable initialises to, it should correspond to the original's near-empty default, not to a moderately heavy shower.

Slow the cloud-glow sawtooth by 1.65x: original period is 6.50 s (ramp 129 -> 255 over ~3.25 s at ~39 counts/s, then hold at full white for ~3.25 s — a 50% duty cycle); the port runs a 3.95 s period (ramp ~90 -> 254 over ~2.6 s at ~64 counts/s, then hold ~1.35 s, ~35% duty). Also raise the reset floor from ~90 to ~129 and let the peak reach 255, not 254. This one is fps-invariant on both sides, so it is a plain timing constant, not a frame-rate issue.

Lightning cadence and duration are the biggest visible gap. The original fires for exactly 21 rendered frames and its inter-flash gaps are integer multiples of that same 21-frame tick; the port fires for a fixed ~0.15 s of wall time with unquantised gaps. At the harness's 20 fps that is 4/min x 1.05 s on the original versus 14-18/min x 0.15 s on the port — a sustained amber wash versus a rapid white strobe. Note the direction: the ORIGINAL is the frame-coupled side here, so the two would roughly converge near 80-140 fps. Either reproduce the original's frame-counted storm tick (fire for 21 render frames, quantise the gap to multiples of that tick, and target ~4 flashes/min at 20 fps), or, if keeping wall-clock timing is deliberate, at minimum lengthen the flash to ~1 s and cut the rate to ~4/min so the harness-rate look matches.

Fix three exact colours, all currently constant and easy to compare: rain drop should be RGB (0,56,255), not (0,8,203) — the port's rain is noticeably darker and less bright; sparkle should be (255,152,0), not (255,107,0) — the port's is too red; and the lightning flash should be the SAME saturated amber (255,152,0) as the sparkles, not the pale peach (255,190,114) the port uses.
Widen the cloud-glow block by ~1.6 px on average: original block length jitters over 7..12 px (mean 9.96) at the tail of a 60 px strip, port over 6..10 px (mean 8.33).

Do NOT change the rain scroll: at -10 px/s toward index 0, fps-invariant, it already matches the original exactly. Sparkle rate (1.02/frame) and its 0/1/2/3/4-per-frame distribution also already match — leave both alone.
